2:1.sourceText: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρνάβα συνπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον·
2:1.targetText: Then after fourteen years again I went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, having also taken Titus with me;

groups.note: The Greek compound taking-along participle contains the accompaniment sense rendered with me; no separate Greek me pronoun is asserted.

2:2.sourceText: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν· καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον.
2:2.targetText: and I went up by revelation, and submitted the good news to them that I preach among the nations, and privately to those esteemed, lest I ran or might run in vain;

groups.note: The Greek present running subjunctive corresponds to the later English might run; the earlier English I ran belongs to the separate Greek past verb ἔδραμον, despite the reversed order.

2:3.sourceText: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί, Ἕλλην ὤν, ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι·
2:3.targetText: but not even Titus, who [is] with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised—

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the who-with-me clause.

2:4.sourceText: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἡμᾶς καταδουλώσουσιν·
2:4.targetText: and [that] because of the false brothers brought in unaware, who came in secretly to spy out our liberty that we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us under bondage,

groups.note: Pinned N1904 has future indicative καταδουλώσουσιν in the purpose clause, while LSV gives might bring under bondage. The enslaving predicate and participants remain shared with mood wording explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English connective supplement at the opening; no corresponding separate Greek demonstrative or conjunction occurs there.

2:5.sourceText: οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ, ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
2:5.targetText: to whom not even for an hour we gave place by subjection, that the truth of the good news might remain to you.

2:6.sourceText: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι, —ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει· πρόσωπον ὁ Θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει— ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο,
2:6.targetText: And from those who were esteemed to be something—whatever they were then, it makes no difference to me. God does not accept the face of man, for to me those esteemed added nothing,

groups.note: The Greek nothing-differs predicate is rendered as the English idiom it makes no difference; the full negated difference predicate is kept together.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

2:7.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς,
2:7.targetText: but on the contrary, having seen that I have been entrusted with the good news of the uncircumcision, as Peter with [that] of the circumcision,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the parallel entrusted-with relation for Peter; the Greek comparison has Peter and the circumcision genitive, without a second written entrusting verb or with preposition.
Bracketed English gospel-object supplement in the elliptical Peter comparison.

2:8.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη,
2:8.targetText: for He who worked with Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, worked also in me in regard to the nations,

groups.note: Greek dative Peter names the recipient/participant of the working; LSV renders with Peter. Its parallel dative ἐμοί is expressed as in me, retaining the two actual participants rather than inventing Greek with/in prepositions.

2:9.sourceText: καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάνης, οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι, δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρνάβα κοινωνίας, ἵνα ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν·
2:9.targetText: and having known the grace that was given to me, James, and Cephas, and John, who were esteemed to be pillars, they gave to me a right hand of fellowship, and to Barnabas, that we may go to the nations, and they to the circumcision,

groups.note: N1904 has plural right hands, δεξιάς; LSV renders the fellowship pledge with singular a right hand. The gesture lexeme is shared with its number difference explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a mission predicate in the Greek elliptical we-to-the-nations clause; no separate Greek going verb is written.

2:10.sourceText: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.
2:10.targetText: only, that we should be mindful of the poor, which I also was diligent—this very thing—to do.

2:11.sourceText: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν.
2:11.targetText: And when Peter came to Antioch, I stood up against him to the face, because he was blameworthy,

groups.note: N1904 names Cephas, Κηφᾶς; LSV names Peter. John1:42 explicitly identifies these Aramaic/Greek names of the same person. The actual Greek name is preserved, not relabeled as the Πέτρος lexeme.

2:12.sourceText: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.
2:12.targetText: for before the coming of some from James, he was eating with the nations, and when they came, he was withdrawing and separating himself, fearing those of circumcision,

2:13.sourceText: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρνάβας συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.
2:13.targetText: and the other Jews acted hypocritically with him, so that Barnabas was also carried away by their hypocrisy.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek also adds the other Jews to the hypocritical action; LSV expresses the other Jews without a separate additive also at that point.

2:14.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς, πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις ἰουδαΐζειν;
2:14.targetText: But when I saw that they are not walking uprightly to the truth of the good news, I said to Peter before all, “If you, being a Jew, live in the manner of the nations, and not in the manner of the Jews, how do you compel the nations to live like Jews?

groups.note: N1904 writes Cephas in the dative; LSV names the same person Peter. The changed name form is explicit, retaining the actual Greek Cephas identity.

targetPhrases.text: in the manner of the nations

groups.note: The adverb ἐθνικῶς is expressed by the whole manner-of-the-nations phrase; no separate Greek manner noun is invented. The parallel Ἰουδαϊκῶς supplies the manner-of-the-Jews phrase.

targetPhrases.text: in the manner of the Jews

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

2:15.sourceText: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί,
2:15.targetText: We by nature Jews, and not sinners of the nations,

2:16.sourceText: εἰδότες δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σάρξ.
2:16.targetText: having also known that a man is not declared righteous by works of law, but through faith from Jesus Christ, we also believed in Christ Jesus, that we might be declared righteous by faith from Christ, and not by works of law, because no flesh will be declared righteous by works of law.”

groups.note: Greek δέ continues the knowing clause; LSV expresses this additive continuation as also.
Greek except/if-not construction qualifies the negated works statement; LSV renders it as the contrasting but-through-faith clause. The whole connective construction is retained.

The Greek genitive of Christ Jesus is rendered by LSV from Jesus Christ, reversing the name order and interpreting the genitive as source. The full genitive name phrase is linked; no separate Greek from preposition is asserted.
The Greek Christ genitive is rendered from Christ by LSV; this is the translation’s interpretation of the genitive relation, not an independently written Greek from preposition.
Greek not...all flesh is the negative-quantifier construction rendered no flesh; both the written negation and universal quantifier jointly anchor English no.

2:17.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος; μὴ γένοιτο.
2:17.targetText: And if, seeking to be declared righteous in Christ, we were also ourselves found sinners, [is] Christ then a servant of sin? Let it not be!

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the Christ-servant-of-sin nominal question.

2:18.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν συνιστάνω.
2:18.targetText: For if the things I threw down, these again I build up, I set myself forth [as] a transgressor;

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English predicative connector supplied before a transgressor.

2:19.sourceText: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα Θεῷ ζήσω· Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι·
2:19.targetText: for I died through law that I may live to God;

unmappedSource.reason: The displayed LSV omits the dative νόμῳ, to law, which is separately written after through law in N1904. It must not be merged into the earlier, different Greek law occurrence.

sourceMoved.reason: Rendered in adjacent LSV 2:20; the group there retains the actual Greek source reference.

2:20.sourceText: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.
2:20.targetText: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me; and that which I now live in the flesh—I live in the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me;

2:21.sourceText: Οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ· εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη, ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν.
2:21.targetText: I do not make the grace of God void, for if righteousness [is] through law—then Christ died in vain.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the righteousness-through-law condition.
